rules.title: Tenant Protection Act just-cause eviction requirement
rules.requirement: Once all tenants have lawfully lived in the unit for 12 months (or at least one tenant for 24 months), your landlord may evict only for a listed at-fault or no-fault just cause, and the cause must be stated in the written termination notice. For a curable lease violation, the landlord must first give you a notice and a chance to fix it.
rules.key_value: Just cause required after 12 months of tenancy (24 months if adult tenants were added)

coverage.summary: Residential rental property statewide, except housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years, owner-occupied duplexes and owner-occupied single-family homes, certain individually owned single-family homes and condos (non-corporate owners who give the required exemption notice), and other listed exemptions. Does not apply where a qualifying local just-cause ordinance covers the unit.
minor_exemptions_not_in_data: Nonprofit hospital, religious, extended care, residential care for the elderly, and adult residential facilities
Dormitories owned by higher education institutions or K-12 schools
Units where the tenant shares bathroom or kitchen with an owner who lives there
Owner-occupied single-family residences renting no more than two units or bedrooms
Single-family homes or condos alienable separately and not owned by a REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member, with written exemption notice

rules.exemptions: Hotels; nonprofit hospitals, religious and care facilities; school dormitories; shared kitchen/bath with resident owner; owner-occupied single-family homes (renting up to two units/bedrooms) and owner-occupied duplexes; housing with certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (unless a mobilehome); separately alienable homes/condos not owned by a REIT, corporation or LLC with a corporate member, if tenants received the statutory exemption notice; deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing; property covered by a qualifying local just-cause ordinance.
rules.penalty: Noncompliant termination notice is void. Owner who attempts to recover possession in material violation is liable for actual damages, discretionary attorney's fees and costs, up to three times actual damages for willful, oppressive, fraudulent or malicious conduct, and punitive damages; Attorney General, city attorney or county counsel may seek injunctive relief.
rules.quoted_span: Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.
rules.interaction: Does not apply to property covered by a local just-cause ordinance adopted on or before September 1, 2019, or a later ordinance that is more protective and contains a binding finding to that effect; a property cannot be subject to both. A local ordinance adopted after September 1, 2019 that is less protective shall not be enforced unless this section is repealed. Current text operative April 1, 2024 and last amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 203 (AB 1529), effective January 1, 2026; repealed as of January 1, 2030. The document does not state when the just-cause requirement first took effect, so effective_date is left null.
rules.conflict_note: State law displaces less-protective local just-cause ordinances adopted after September 1, 2019 while yielding to earlier or more-protective local ordinances; local coverage must be checked.

rules.title: Relocation assistance for no-fault just-cause terminations
rules.requirement: If your landlord ends a covered tenancy for a no-fault reason (owner move-in, withdrawal from the rental market, a government order, or demolition or substantial remodel), they must either pay you one month's rent as relocation assistance within 15 calendar days of the notice or waive your final month's rent in writing. The notice must tell you about this right; if the landlord does not strictly comply, the notice is void.
rules.key_value: 1 month rent (direct payment within 15 days or final-month rent waiver)

coverage.summary: Tenancies requiring just cause under Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2(a) that are terminated for a no-fault just cause; same building coverage and exemptions as the statewide just-cause rule.
minor_exemptions_not_in_data: Nonprofit hospital, religious, and care facilities
Shared kitchen or bath with resident owner
Single-family homes or condos not owned by a REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member, with exemption notice

rules.exemptions: Same exemptions as Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2(e); no relocation assistance if a government agency or court finds the tenant at fault for the condition triggering a vacate order.
rules.penalty: Owner's failure to strictly comply renders the notice of termination void; relocation paid is recoverable as damages if tenant fails to vacate.
rules.quoted_span: The amount of relocation assistance or rent waiver shall be equal to one month of the tenant’s rent that was in effect when the owner issued the notice to terminate the tenancy.
rules.interaction: Relocation assistance under this section is credited against any other relocation assistance required by other law. Does not apply to property governed by a qualifying local just-cause ordinance. Current text operative April 1, 2024, amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 203 (AB 1529), effective January 1, 2026.

notes: Official statutory text of Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2 (Tenant Protection Act just cause). The section's operative date (April 1, 2024) and latest amendment (Stats. 2025, Ch. 203, eff. Jan 1, 2026) date re-enactments, not the rule's start, so effective_date is null. Section sunsets January 1, 2030. The notice-content requirements (owner move-in and remodel notice contents, tenant-rights disclosure) were not recorded separately as they govern notice form. No rent-increase coverage stated beyond a cross-reference to § 1947.12.
